As of July 26, Nvidia's supply and capacity commitment amount reached $279 billion, more than double the $119 billion disclosed in the prior quarter.
Nvidia also disclosed an additional $36 billion of cloud‑service commitments from providers purchasing its hardware.
In its latest quarterly filing, Nvidia warned that infrastructure shortages could delay chip purchases and hurt revenue, and that some supply commitments may be adjusted or cancelled.
Analysts are divided on the outlook for data‑center construction
Research firm SemiAnalysis is more optimistic, noting that 40 sites with a combined capacity of over 24GW are now in relatively mature construction phases.
The firm’s researchers wrote on Monday, "Large campuses are indeed being built, and many projects are on schedule."
Delays in data‑center completion do not necessarily mean Nvidia will lose those chip sales; the chips could be resold to customers with sufficient power.
Goldberg himself expects Nvidia’s sales to hit a new peak before early 2027, but he sees the related risk rising over the next year.

On Polymarket, the probability that Nvidia will be the world’s most valuable company by the end of 2026 was above 80% earlier this month, but Friday morning data showed it had fallen to 56%, while Apple (AAPL-US) rose to 41%.

items.title: AI需求爆棚卻缺錢！黃仁勳：資金需求遠超供給 新型雲端業者融資受考驗
items.title_en: AI Demand Booms but Money Is Short! Jensen Huang: Funding Needs Far Outstrip Supply, New Cloud Providers Face Financing Test
paras: 《CNBC》週五 (23 日) 報導，輝達 (NVDA-US) 柏林 GTC 大會展現人工智慧 (AI) 基礎建設的龐大商機，但場邊討論也浮現另一層隱憂：隨著業者大舉借貸擴建，資金供給能否跟上投資需求，正成為產業關注焦點。輝達執行長黃仁勳直言，市場對資金的需求遠高於目前可取得的規模。
柏林 GTC 是黃仁勳為期約一週半歐洲行的重要壓軸。他 21 日在行程中會晤多國領袖、發表新產品，也在台上與小型機器鴨互動。不過，熱鬧的展示之外，與會的 AI 基礎建設業者、投資人及資料中心供應商，談論的重點包括新型雲端業者的財務壓力、小型資料中心部署，以及資金取得難度。
大會最後一天，提供 AI 算力租賃服務的新型雲端業者 (neocloud) 股價再遭重挫。
CoreWeave (CRWV-US) 週四 (22日) 收跌約 10%，Nebius (NBIS-US) 下跌約 7%，延續近期因高額借貸引發疑慮的震盪走勢。
一名 AI 基礎建設公司主管表示，大量尚無信用評等的企業投入這個市場，正讓投資人感到不安。
黃仁勳對需求前景仍抱持樂觀看法。他表示，從基本面來看，市場對新型雲端業者的需求極為強勁。不過，輝達也持有多家相關公司的股權，是這波算力擴張的重要參與者。
如何加快算力上線，是這次大會的另一項主軸。
黃仁勳發表DSX POD，將Vera Rubin運算系統、網路、供電與液冷設備預先整合於模組化貨櫃，將7座Vera Rubin AI機櫃裝進一個貨櫃，並在工廠完成組裝與測試後出貨，並可透過一般道路運輸，藉此縮短部署時間，最快可於 14天 內完成部署並投入運作。
黃仁勳指出，資料中心延後啟用，可能造成數十億美元營收損失。若能將更多整合工作提前移至供應鏈完成，就有望加快設施上線速度。
大型算力需求者也開始尋找較小規模的部署機會。 9 月媒體引述消息人士報導，OpenAI 與 Anthropic 正洽尋較小型的 AI 資料中心交易，以取得所需算力。
然而，加快部署仍須龐大資金支撐。高盛估計，2026 年至 2031 年間，涵蓋運算、資料中心與電力的 AI 相關資本支出，合計可能達約 7.6 兆美元。黃仁勳則在週三的大會上表示，一座 1 吉瓦 (GW) 資料中心的建置成本約為 500 億美元。
黃仁勳週四接受訪問時指出，目前缺少的是支撐成長所需的營運資金。由於 AI 各領域同時出現龐大需求，資金供給因此吃緊。
「資金需求遠大於可取得的資金。」黃仁勳表示，但他也相信，這個問題最終會獲得解決。
一名 AI 基礎建設融資公司的主管表示，資金很快就會成為產業發展的瓶頸。隨著算力需求持續擴張，業者除了設法取得晶片、電力與機房，也必須證明自己有能力籌措並承擔建設所需的資金。
paras_en: CNBC reported on Friday (the 23rd) that Nvidia's (NVDA-US) GTC conference in Berlin showcased the massive business opportunity in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, but side‑stage discussions also revealed another concern: as companies borrow heavily to expand, can capital supply keep up with investment demand, which is becoming a focal point for the industry. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said outright that the market's demand for funding far exceeds the amount currently available.

The Berlin GTC is the centerpiece of Jensen Huang's roughly week‑and‑a‑half European tour. On the 21st he met multiple national leaders, unveiled new products, and even interacted onstage with a small robot duck. Beyond the lively demos, AI infrastructure firms, investors and data‑center suppliers at the event focused on the financial pressure on new‑type cloud providers, the deployment of small data centers, and the difficulty of securing capital.
On the final day of the conference, the stock of a new‑type cloud provider offering AI compute‑rental services (neocloud) tumbled again.
CoreWeave (CRWV-US) fell about 10% on Thursday (the 22nd) and Nebius (NBIS-US) dropped roughly 7%, continuing the recent volatility sparked by concerns over large‑scale borrowing.
An executive at an AI infrastructure company said that a flood of firms without credit ratings entering the market is unsettling investors.

Jensen Huang remains optimistic about demand prospects. He said that fundamentally, demand for new‑type cloud providers is extremely strong. Nvidia also holds equity stakes in several related companies, making it a key participant in this wave of compute expansion.
Accelerating the rollout of compute capacity was another key theme of the conference.

Jensen Huang unveiled the DSX POD, which pre‑integrates the Vera Rubin computing system, networking, power and liquid‑cooling equipment into a modular container. Seven Vera Rubin AI cabinets are packed into a single container, assembled and tested at the factory, then shipped and road‑transportable, shortening deployment time to as fast as 14 days from shipment to operation.

Huang noted that delayed data‑center activation could cost tens of billions of dollars in revenue. If more integration work is shifted upstream to the supply chain, facility rollout speed could be accelerated.

Large compute users are also looking for smaller‑scale deployment opportunities. Media reports in September quoted sources saying OpenAI and Anthropic are negotiating for smaller AI data‑center deals to secure the needed compute.

However, faster deployment still requires massive capital. Goldman Sachs estimates AI‑related capital expenditures—including compute, data centers and power—could total about $7.6 trillion between 2026 and 2031. Huang said at Wednesday’s event that building a 1‑gigawatt data center costs roughly $50 billion.
In an interview on Thursday, Huang said the current shortage is operating capital needed to support growth. With huge demand across AI sectors, funding is becoming tight.
"Funding demand far exceeds the capital that can be obtained," Huang said, but he believes the issue will eventually be resolved.

An executive at an AI infrastructure financing firm warned that capital will soon become a bottleneck for industry development. As compute demand keeps expanding, companies must not only secure chips, power and facilities, but also demonstrate they can raise and bear the financing required for construction.

items.title: 偶遇馬雲成轉折 黑石豪押AI全產業鏈
items.title_en: A Chance Encounter with Jack Ma Marks a Turning Point as Blackstone Makes a Massive Bet on the AI Industry Chain
paras: 黑石集團（Blackstone）執行長蘇世民（Steve Schwarzman）透露，公司如今大舉押注人工智慧（AI），源於十多年前一次與阿里巴巴創辦人馬雲的偶然相遇。
蘇世民接受彭博電視台「Leaders With Francine Lacqua」節目採訪時回憶，2015年，他在中國搭乘客運時，恰好坐在馬雲旁邊。馬雲當時主動談起AI，但蘇世民坦言：「說實話，我當時完全不知道他在講什麼。」
馬雲向他解釋，AI將是影響最深遠的技術變革，並改變整個世界。這場交談後來成為黑石調整投資方向的重要契機。
如今，這家管理約1.3兆美元資產的另類投資巨頭，已將AI布局延伸至資料中心、能源、晶片融資、企業股權及投資決策等多個領域。
黑石管理的資料中心資產規模約達2,000億美元，並與Google(GOOGL-US)合作開展雲端運算業務。公司也持有OpenAI等AI實驗室的股份，並以博通(AVGO-US)和輝達(NVDA-US)的晶片為基礎開展融資業務。
除了運算基礎設施與晶片，黑石也投資發電廠及資料中心散熱設備，布局支撐AI運算所需的關鍵環節。
在企業應用方面，黑石透過旗下數百家企業推廣AI技術，相關工作主要由Ode負責。Ode是一家企業諮詢公司，由黑石與Anthropic、私募股權公司Hellman & Friedman及其他投資者合作創立。
AI也進入黑石內部的投資流程。AI模型如今已參與評估潛在投資項目，成為分析交易的工具之一。
從基礎設施到企業應用，黑石試圖從AI產業鏈的不同環節尋找投資機會，但布局越廣，也意味著風險可能跨越多種資產類別。
資料中心擴張遇阻 AI投資風險升溫
身為美國規模最大的商業資料中心業主，黑石正面臨日益升高的政治與社會壓力。
隨著外界對工作機會流失、AI失控風險及資料中心高耗電問題的擔憂加深，相關建設遭遇更多反對聲浪，黑石部分項目也受到阻礙。
資本市場的疑慮則集中在AI支出能否持續。隨著黑石、阿波羅全球管理公司、Brookfield Asset Management及KKR等大型資產管理業者持續加碼AI，投資者可能在股票、信貸及基礎設施等不同資產中，反覆承擔相同的AI投資風險。
一旦AI投資週期逆轉，衝擊可能同時傳導至多個市場。換言之，布局多個產業環節，不代表就能真正分散風險。
蘇世民：重大技術變革需數十年才能兌現價值
面對AI投資可能過熱的疑慮，蘇世民認為，重大技術創新往往需要數十年才能充分展現經濟價值，初期投入不一定能迅速轉化為利潤。
他以電力基礎設施為例指出，愛迪生於1882年發明電燈泡，但要讓電燈泡真正發揮作用，仍需要建設完整的電網，而這個過程花了約40年。
蘇世民表示，「當時還沒有人了解廣播，也沒有人了解電視。建設電網時，沒有人會想到這些應用。」
電網最初是為電燈泡等用途而建設，後來卻成為廣播、電視等新興產業發展的基礎。蘇世民認為，AI目前也處於發展早期，未來的應用範圍與商業價值仍可能持續擴大。
他表示，「而我們現在還處於這一進程的早期階段。」
這也是黑石長期投資AI基礎設施的核心思路：即使部分項目短期回報有限，底層設施仍可能隨技術發展而產生更廣泛的價值。不過，長期前景並不保證每項投資都能獲利，資本支出、能源成本與實際需求之間的平衡，仍是投資者必須面對的考驗。
談美國政治極化 蘇世民籲回到中間地帶
採訪中，蘇世民也談及美國日益加劇的政治分歧。身為長期共和黨支持者，他表示，不同政治陣營之間的距離越來越遠，跨陣營溝通也變得更加困難。
他談到，「我認為，如今無論身處哪個政黨都不容易。過去，社會中間地帶曾經相當廣闊，而我就屬於這一部分。」
他接著表示，「如今，我們已經走到了人們不再願意傾聽彼此的地步。我認為這非常令人遺憾，也給整個國家帶來了挑戰。我們需要重新回到一個更加平衡的中間地帶。」
從與馬雲的一次偶遇，到如今橫跨資料中心、雲端運算、晶片融資及能源基礎設施的投資布局，黑石的AI策略已遠遠超出單純投資科技股的範疇。
蘇世民押注AI的長期潛力，但隨著資料中心建設阻力增加、資本支出持續攀升，以及市場對投資集中風險的疑慮升溫，黑石仍須證明，對AI產業鏈的全面布局能否轉化為持續且合理的投資回報。
paras_en: Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman disclosed that the firm’s current large‑scale bet on artificial intelligence (AI) stems from a chance encounter with Alibaba founder Jack Ma more than a decade ago.

Schwarzman recalled on Bloomberg Television’s “Leaders With Francine Lacqua” that in 2015, while riding a bus in China, he happened to sit next to Jack Ma. Ma proactively brought up AI, but Schwarzman admitted, “To be honest, I had no idea what he was talking about at the time.”

Ma explained that AI would be the most far‑reaching technological transformation and would change the entire world. That conversation later became a key catalyst for Blackstone to adjust its investment direction.

Today, the alternative‑investment giant that manages roughly $1.3 trillion in assets has extended its AI footprint into data centers, energy, chip financing, corporate equity and investment‑decision processes among other areas.

Blackstone’s data‑center assets total about $200 billion and it partners with Google (GOOGL‑US) on cloud‑computing services. The firm also holds stakes in AI labs such as OpenAI and conducts financing activities based on chips from Broadcom (AVGO‑US) and Nvidia (NVDA‑US).
Beyond compute infrastructure and chips, Blackstone is investing in power plants and data‑center cooling equipment, positioning itself in the critical links needed to support AI workloads.

On the enterprise‑application side, Blackstone promotes AI technology through hundreds of portfolio companies, with the work largely handled by Ode. Ode is a consulting firm co‑founded by Blackstone, Anthropic, private‑equity firm Hellman & Friedman and other investors.
AI has also entered Blackstone’s internal investment process. AI models now participate in evaluating potential deals, becoming one of the tools used to analyze transactions.

From infrastructure to enterprise applications, Blackstone is seeking investment opportunities across different segments of the AI value chain, but the broader the exposure, the more the risk can span multiple asset classes.
Data‑center expansion faces headwinds, raising AI‑investment risk
As the United States’ largest commercial data‑center owner, Blackstone is confronting growing political and social pressure.

With mounting concerns over job losses, AI‑runaway risks and the high electricity consumption of data centers, construction projects are meeting increasing opposition and some Blackstone projects are being stalled.

Capital‑market worries focus on whether AI spending can be sustained. As Blackstone, Apollo Global Management, Brookfield Asset Management and KKR and other large asset managers keep ramping up AI exposure, investors may repeatedly assume the same AI risk across equities, credit and infrastructure assets.

If the AI investment cycle reverses, the shock could transmit to multiple markets simultaneously. In other words, spreading across many industry segments does not necessarily mean true risk diversification.
Schwarzman: Major technological shifts take decades to deliver value

Addressing concerns that AI investment may be overheating, Schwarzman said that major technological innovations often need several decades to fully realize economic value, and early‑stage spending does not always translate quickly into profit.

He cited electricity infrastructure as an example, noting that Thomas Edison invented the light bulb in 1882, but it took about 40 years to build the power grid needed for the bulb to become truly useful.
Schwarzman added, “Back then no one understood broadcasting, no one understood television. When the grid was being built, no one could foresee those applications.”

The grid was initially built for lighting and similar uses, but later became the foundation for emerging industries such as broadcasting and television. Schwarzman believes AI is similarly in an early stage, and its future applications and commercial value could continue to expand.
He said, “We are still in the early phase of this process.”

That is the core logic behind Blackstone’s long‑term investment in AI infrastructure: even if some projects deliver limited short‑term returns, the underlying facilities may generate broader value as the technology matures. However, long‑term prospects do not guarantee profit on every investment; balancing capital outlays, energy costs and actual demand remains a test for investors.
Discussing U.S. political polarization, Schwarzman calls for a return to the middle ground

In the interview, Schwarzman also spoke about the growing political divide in the United States. As a long‑time Republican supporter, he said the distance between political camps is widening and cross‑camp communication is becoming increasingly difficult.
He noted, “I think it’s hard for anyone in any party these days. In the past, the middle of society was quite broad, and I was part of that.”

He continued, “Now we have reached a point where people no longer want to listen to each other. I find that very regrettable and it poses a challenge for the whole country. We need to get back to a more balanced middle ground.”

From a single chance meeting with Jack Ma to an investment portfolio that spans data centers, cloud computing, chip financing and energy infrastructure, Blackstone’s AI strategy now goes far beyond merely buying tech stocks.

Schwarzman is betting on AI’s long‑term potential, but as data‑center construction faces more resistance, capital spending keeps climbing, and concerns over concentrated investment risk rise, Blackstone still has to prove that its comprehensive AI‑value‑chain approach can translate into sustained and reasonable investment returns.

items.title: 散戶抄底愈抄愈低！半導體槓桿ETF單周吸金61億美元 10月已暴跌逾40%
items.title_en: Retail Investors' Bottom‑Fishing Gets Deeper: Semiconductor Leveraged ETF Pulls in $6.1 B in One Week, Down Over 40% in October
paras: 人工智慧(AI)交易近期再度受挫，投資人上周試圖趁股價下跌進場，把資金投入一檔高風險槓桿型指數股票型基金(ETF)，以放大半導體股的每日報酬，但在晶片股賣壓依然沉重的情況下，試圖逢低買進的投資人也面臨虧損。
根據FactSet數據，追蹤熱門半導體指數每日漲跌幅三倍的「Direxion每日三倍做多半導體ETF」(Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF)(SOXL-US)，上周吸引創紀錄的61億美元資金流入。
然而，半導體股本周持續下跌，FactSet數據顯示，這檔槓桿ETF本周再跌10.8%，連續第三周下跌，10月迄今跌幅可能已超過43%。
換句話說，投資人原本想逢低買進，沒想到股價卻持續探底。

槓桿ETF單日重挫逾2成 AI投資回報疑慮升高

FactSet數據顯示，這檔槓桿ETF本周到周四持續有資金流入，然而周四當天半導體股遭到猛烈拋售，ETF股價也大幅下挫。
AI交易這個月每天都劇烈波動，足以左右標普500指數單日表現，令投資人感到不安。
財富管理公司Glenmede投資策略副總裁Mike Reynolds周五(23日)說：「半導體股對AI基建設置的變化極為敏感。市場目前已開始對AI交易抱持懷疑。」
投資人高度關注AI發展需要的大量晶片，使半導體公司今年來股價大幅上漲。強勁的AI晶片需求推動相關企業獲利成長，但投資人也密切關注企業的AI支出，擔心如此積極的投資步調可能難以持續。
半導體股大幅波動，也帶動投資人對槓桿ETF的熱情。這類基金利用衍生性金融商品放大股市每日報酬，但若投資人將其當作押注股價上漲的交易工具，一旦市場反向下跌，可能蒙受沉重損失。
根據FactSet數據，Direxion每日三倍做多半導體ETF周四當天重挫20.5%，創6月23日以來最差單日表現。相較之下，iShares半導體ETF(iShares Semiconductor ETF)(SOXX-US)當日下跌6.8%，跌幅較小。
FactSet數據顯示，Direxion每日三倍做多半導體ETF本月周線表現持續疲弱，截至周五已連續第三周下跌。

半導體股今年仍大漲 投資人重新評估估值

在半導體股2026年大幅上漲後，投資人正重新評估相關股票的估值。iShares半導體ETF今年以來仍大漲近59%，儘管近期半導體股再度承受賣壓。
Reynolds說：「在目前這樣的估值水準，以及經歷如此猛烈的漲勢後，投資人冷靜重新評估這項AI主題可能帶來的投資回報，是件好事。」
他也表示，投資人在市場真正陷入狂熱、股價與基本面完全脫節之前，就開始即時質疑這波行情，是有益的。
FactSet數據顯示，美股周五收低，標普500資訊科技類股連續第三周下跌，創3月以來最長連續周線跌勢。iShares半導體ETF也連續第三周下跌，10月跌幅可能達15.9%。
paras_en: AI‑driven trading has hit another snag recently. Last week investors tried to capitalize on falling prices by pouring money into a high‑risk leveraged semiconductor index fund to amplify daily returns, but with chip stocks still under heavy selling pressure, those buying the dip are also facing losses.

According to FactSet data, the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL‑US), which tracks a popular semiconductor index with three‑times daily price movements, attracted a record $6.1 billion of inflows last week.

However, semiconductor stocks kept sliding this week. FactSet shows the leveraged ETF fell another 10.8% this week, marking a third consecutive week of decline, and its October loss may already exceed 43%.
In other words, investors who hoped to buy the dip found the price continuing to plunge.

The leveraged ETF saw a single‑day plunge of over 20%, raising doubts about AI‑driven returns. FactSet data indicate that while inflows continued through Thursday, semiconductor stocks were hammered that day, dragging the ETF’s price sharply lower.
AI‑related trading has been wildly volatile all month, enough to sway the S&P 500’s daily performance and leave investors uneasy.

Mike Reynolds, vice‑president of investment strategy at wealth‑management firm Glenmede, said on Friday the 23rd that semiconductor stocks are extremely sensitive to changes in AI infrastructure spending, and the market is now growing skeptical of AI‑driven trading.

Investors have been closely watching the massive chip demand required for AI development, which has driven semiconductor shares sharply higher this year. Strong AI chip demand has boosted earnings for related firms, but investors are also watching corporate AI spending, fearing such aggressive investment may be hard to sustain.

The wild swings in semiconductor stocks have also fueled enthusiasm for leveraged ETFs. These funds use derivatives to magnify daily market returns, but if investors treat them as bets on price rises, a market reversal can inflict heavy losses.

FactSet data show the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF plunged 20.5% on Thursday, its worst single‑day performance since June 23. By contrast, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX‑US) fell 6.8% that day, a much smaller drop.
FactSet indicates the leveraged ETF’s weekly performance has remained weak this month, and by Friday it had logged a third consecutive week of decline.

Semiconductor stocks have surged dramatically this year, prompting investors to reassess valuations. The iShares Semiconductor ETF is up nearly 59% year‑to‑date, even as recent selling pressure returns to chip stocks.
Reynolds said that given current valuation levels and the recent fierce rally, it is healthy for investors to calmly re‑evaluate the potential returns of the AI theme.
He added that it is beneficial for investors to question the rally in real time before the market becomes overly frothy and prices diverge completely from fundamentals.

FactSet data show U.S. equities closed lower on Friday, with the S&P 500 information‑technology sector posting its third consecutive weekly decline—the longest streak since March. The iShares Semiconductor ETF also fell for a third straight week, with an October decline that could reach 15.9%.

items.title: 《路透》揭密：美政府多年要求馬斯克調整烏克蘭星鏈服務
items.title_en: Reuters Reveals: U.S. Government Years of Demands for Musk to Adjust Starlink Service in Ukraine
paras: 《路透》週五 (23 日) 報導，早在烏克蘭本月遭限制使用衛星通訊服務之前，拜登與川普政府就曾多次要求馬斯克旗下 SpaceX，配合外交與國安政策，調整烏克蘭、伊朗及中東其他地區的星鏈 (Starlink) 服務，包括擴大服務範圍，以及停用疑似落入武裝組織手中的終端設備。
這些過往未曝光的互動，正值烏克蘭衛星服務遭限速之際浮上檯面，也凸顯美國執行外交與國安政策時，對 SpaceX 的高度依賴。
根據熟悉內情的美國前高階官員說法，拜登政府曾要求 SpaceX，停用疑似流入葉門青年運動 (Houthi) 與黎巴嫩真主黨手中的星鏈終端設備，也曾要求擴大烏克蘭軍方使用星鏈的範圍，並協助伊朗民眾取得網路連線。
據多名前官員透露，拜登政府與 SpaceX 的協調通常涉及五角大廈及白宮官員，其中一項重點，是防止美國對手使用透過中間人取得的星鏈設備。
2023 年 10 月，以色列與真主黨在黎巴嫩南部交戰期間，美國情報官員向白宮通報，與真主黨有關的人士可能已取得星鏈終端設備。2024 年美國對葉門青年運動發動空襲期間，官員也有類似疑慮。
在這兩起事件中，拜登政府均要求 SpaceX 辨識並停用相關設備。
2 名前官員表示，至少部分終端設備後來確實遭到停用。
SpaceX 在 2024 年提交美國商務部工業暨安全局的文件中表示，公司與美國政府機關密切合作，在必要時取得出口授權，並保護相關技術，以支持美國國安與外交政策目標。
另一方面，俄羅斯於 2022 年全面入侵烏克蘭後，拜登政府曾推動 SpaceX 擴大烏軍使用星鏈。
同年 9 月，伊朗女子 Mahsa Amini 因頭巾穿戴問題遭逮捕後死亡，引發示威浪潮，拜登政府也曾要求 SpaceX 在伊朗提供星鏈服務，並協助將終端設備送入當地。
川普政府則在美國與以色列於 2025 年及 2026 年攻擊伊朗後，與馬斯克及 SpaceX 討論將星鏈終端設備送入伊朗並啟用，希望改善反政府示威者的網路與通訊能力。不過，川普政府與 SpaceX 均未公開證實，相關設備是否已啟用。
雖然歷屆美國政府都曾仰賴 SpaceX 協助執行政策，華府與馬斯克之間卻並非始終步調一致。
《路透》先前報導，馬斯克曾於 2022 年下令，停止在烏軍試圖收復的部分地區提供星鏈服務，令白宮官員感到意外。他也曾公開表示，拒絕烏方要求在克里米亞塞凡堡啟用星鏈、協助攻擊俄羅斯艦隊，理由是擔心捲入重大戰爭行動。
如今，烏克蘭衛星服務遭限速，再度引發外界對相關決策權歸屬的關注。
烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基上週表示，軍用衛星通訊系統星盾 (Starshield) 的使用受到刻意限制，影響烏軍無人機運作；烏克蘭用於部分軍事任務、包括防禦俄羅斯飛彈攻擊的星鏈服務，也遭到降速。
澤倫斯基週五再度表示，烏克蘭使用星鏈服務所受的限制尚未完全解除。
美國總統川普週五說，會去了解情況；他之前聽說問題已經解決，但如果還沒解決，他會跟馬斯克談。
SpaceX 未回應置評要求。
馬斯克本週稍早則在社群平台表示，星盾系統由美國政府擁有及控制，任何速度或使用限制，都由美軍決定，最終決策權在美國總統手中。
烏克蘭駐美大使館發言人 Halyna Yusypiuk 表示，烏方首要之務是讓服務儘速恢復正常速度，因為「我們人民的生命仰賴這項服務」。
星鏈已成為烏軍前線部隊之間的重要通訊工具，烏軍表示，目前尚無其他產品能提供同等能力。抗無線電干擾能力較強的星盾接收設備，則用於無人機機載導引及遠端操控連線，支援烏軍在烏克蘭境內俄軍防線後方執行任務。
烏克蘭遭限速，也讓部分歐洲官員更加主張建立自主軍用衛星通訊能力，但短期內仍缺乏可行的替代方案。
美國民主黨眾議員 Jason Crow 週五要求釐清烏克蘭衛星服務調整的來龍去脈，並警告美國依賴 SpaceX 的風險。他表示，未經選舉產生的億萬富豪與民間企業，不應決定什麼符合美國國安利益。
衛星產業顧問公司 Summit Ridge Group 總裁 Armand Musey 表示，馬斯克身為承接政府合約的企業執行長，實際上卻對重大外交政策決策具有影響力，而外界往往難以判斷，他的決定究竟出於個人考量，還是受到其他因素左右。
paras_en: Reuters reported on Friday (the 23rd) that long before Ukraine was restricted from using satellite communications this month, both the Biden and Trump administrations repeatedly asked SpaceX, owned by Elon Musk, to adjust Starlink service in Ukraine, Iran and other Middle‑East regions in line with diplomatic and national‑security policies, including expanding coverage and disabling terminals suspected of falling into the hands of armed groups.

These previously undisclosed interactions have come to light as Ukraine’s satellite service faces throttling, highlighting the heavy reliance on SpaceX when the United States implements its diplomatic and security policies.

According to former senior U.S. officials familiar with the matter, the Biden administration asked SpaceX to disable Starlink terminals believed to be in the possession of Yemen’s Houthi movement and Lebanon’s Hezbollah, to broaden the Ukrainian military’s use of Starlink, and to help Iranian civilians obtain internet connectivity.

Multiple former officials said coordination between the Biden administration and SpaceX typically involved Pentagon and White House officials, with a key focus on preventing U.S. adversaries from using Starlink equipment obtained through intermediaries.

In October 2023, during fighting between Israel and Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, U.S. intelligence warned the White House that individuals linked to Hezbollah may have obtained Starlink terminals. Similar concerns were raised by officials during the U.S. air campaign against Yemen’s Houthi movement in 2024.
In both incidents, the Biden administration instructed SpaceX to identify and deactivate the relevant terminals.
Two former officials said that at least some of the terminals were indeed taken offline later.

In filings to the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security for 2024, SpaceX stated that it works closely with U.S. government agencies, obtains export authorizations when needed, and safeguards related technology to support U.S. national‑security and diplomatic objectives.
On the other hand, after Russia’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Biden administration pushed SpaceX to expand Starlink use by Ukrainian forces.

In September of that year, after the death of Iranian woman Mahsa Amini sparked protests, the Biden administration also asked SpaceX to provide Starlink service in Iran and to help get terminals into the country.

The Trump administration, after the United States and Israel attacked Iran in 2025 and 2026, discussed with Musk and SpaceX the delivery and activation of Starlink terminals in Iran to improve internet and communications for anti‑government protesters, though neither the Trump administration nor SpaceX publicly confirmed whether the equipment was ever activated.
Although successive U.S. governments have relied on SpaceX to implement policy, Washington’s relationship with Musk has not always been in lockstep.

Reuters previously reported that Musk ordered a halt to Starlink service in parts of territory the Ukrainian army was trying to retake in 2022, surprising White House officials. He has also publicly refused Ukrainian requests to activate Starlink in Crimea’s Sevastopol or to assist attacks on the Russian navy, citing concerns about becoming embroiled in major combat operations.
Now that Ukraine’s satellite service is being throttled, attention has turned again to who ultimately decides such policies.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said last week that the use of the military satellite communications system Starshield is being deliberately limited, affecting drone operations, and that Starlink service used for certain military tasks, including defending against Russian missile attacks, has also been slowed.
Zelensky reiterated on Friday that the restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starlink have not been fully lifted.
President Trump said on Friday he would look into the situation; he had heard the issue was resolved, but if it was not, he would discuss it with Musk.
SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment.

Earlier this week Musk posted on social media that the Starshield system is owned and controlled by the U.S. government, that any speed or usage limits are set by the U.S. military, and that ultimate decision‑making authority rests with the U.S. president.
Ukrainian Embassy spokesperson Halyna Yusypiuk said Ukraine’s top priority is to restore the service to normal speed as “the lives of our people depend on it.”

Starlink has become a vital communications tool for Ukrainian frontline troops, who say no other product currently offers comparable capability. The more jam‑resistant Starshield receivers are used for drone onboard guidance and remote‑control links, supporting Ukrainian operations behind Russian lines inside Ukraine.
The throttling in Ukraine has prompted some European officials to push harder for an independent military satellite communications capability, though viable short‑term alternatives remain lacking.

Democratic Representative Jason Crow demanded on Friday that the full story behind the adjustments to Ukraine’s satellite service be clarified and warned of the risks of U.S. reliance on SpaceX. He argued that an unelected billionaire and private company should not decide what serves U.S. national‑security interests.

Armand Musey, president of the satellite‑industry consultancy Summit Ridge Group, said that while Musk, as CEO of a government‑contracting firm, wields influence over major diplomatic decisions, it is often difficult for outsiders to discern whether his choices stem from personal considerations or other pressures.

items.title: 英國砸1億英鎊建AI生物安全實驗室 OpenAI、Anthropic助陣
items.title_en: UK Allocates £100 Million to Build AI Biosecurity Lab, Backed by OpenAI and Anthropic
paras: 英國政府宣布將撥款 1 億英鎊（約 1.34 億美元）成立「人工智慧生物安全實驗室」（AI Biosecurity Lab），並獲得 OpenAI、Anthropic 與 Google DeepMind 等巨頭支援。此計畫為英國政府提升 AI 風險理解與應對能力的一連串新舉措之一。
官方聲明指出，該實驗室將運用 AI 來偵測與監控生物威脅，OpenAI 與 Anthropic 亦將額外提供高達 2 億英鎊的 AI 模型算力額度。
此外，實驗室將與 Google DeepMind 及生命科學企業 Basecamp Research 展開合作，政府同時也另撥款 6,500 萬英鎊用於研發病原體對策。
英國 AI 技術大臣納拉揚（Kanishka Narayan）表示，隨著 AI 技術日益強大，英國必須具備保護國民並塑造自身未來的能力，這意味著在建構攸關國家安全的核心技術之際，必須在網路攻擊與生物風險等新興威脅上保持領先。
他補充指出，該實驗室將成為一座重大的全新國際機構，匯聚全球頂尖科學專業，除保護大眾免受新興生物威脅外，亦確保英國在 AI 安全與防護領域保持全球領先地位。
實驗室的成立，讓英國政府的AI策略日益清晰：在現有政府部門之外設立機構，針對這項技術的不同面向進行研究、監測與應用。
本次發布的計畫還包含向「AI 安全研究所」（AI Safety Institute）追加 1.2 億英鎊資金，該單位為目前預算最充裕、專注於定期評估尖端 AI 模型的政府機構；此外亦向即將成立、旨在分析 AI 對經濟影響的「AI 經濟研究所」（AI Economics Institute）注入 2,300 萬英鎊資金。
這項策略是英國力求在AI領域維持影響力的關鍵。儘管英國在最先進的AI模型發展上落後美國與中國，仍試圖在監測與監管方面扮演「公正中間人」，走出一條有別於歐盟強力監管科技的路線。
Anthropic國際事務主管Matt Clifford表示：「AI正在改變我們面臨的生物風險，也改變生物領域探索的方式。我們讚許英國政府成立AI生物安全實驗室的遠見。」Clifford曾擔任英國首相的AI顧問，直到去年6月卸任。
他強調，將頂尖 AI、英國的強大科研實力與政府專業相結合，提早偵測威脅並加速醫療方案的研發，將有助於 AI 技術在產業與社會中的安全導入。
另一方面，為防範全球政府與企業日前急忙修補由 AI 協助發現的兩項廣泛應用技術之重大漏洞，英國政府亦宣布撥款 1.3 億英鎊，運用 AI 來辨識關鍵基礎設施與經濟體系中的網路漏洞，以強化國家的資安防禦。
此外，主權AI基金（Sovereign AI Fund）將獲增資1.2億英鎊，將投資範圍擴大至機器人、自主系統及先進製造等實體與工業AI領域，並擴大向英國新創企業採購的計畫。
paras_en: The UK government announced it will allocate £100 million (about $134 million) to establish an "Artificial Intelligence Biosecurity Lab," with support from giants such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. The initiative is one of a series of new measures aimed at enhancing the government's understanding of AI risks and its response capabilities.
The official statement says the lab will use AI to detect and monitor biological threats, and OpenAI and Anthropic will also provide up to £200 million in AI model compute credits.
In addition, the lab will partner with Google DeepMind and life‑science company Basecamp Research, while the government is earmarking another £65 million for research on pathogen countermeasures.

UK AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said that as AI technology becomes increasingly powerful, the UK must have the capacity to protect its citizens and shape its own future, which means staying ahead of emerging threats such as cyber attacks and biological risks while building core technologies critical to national security.

He added that the lab will become a major new international institution, bringing together top scientists worldwide to protect the public from emerging biological threats and to ensure the UK remains a global leader in AI safety and protection.

The creation of the lab clarifies the UK government's AI strategy: establishing a dedicated entity outside existing ministries to research, monitor and apply the technology across its various dimensions.

The announcement also includes an additional £120 million for the AI Safety Institute, the best‑funded government body that regularly evaluates cutting‑edge AI models, and £23 million for a soon‑to‑be‑launched AI Economics Institute that will analyze AI’s impact on the economy.

The strategy is key to the UK’s effort to maintain influence in AI. Although it lags behind the US and China in developing the most advanced models, it seeks to act as a "fair intermediary" in monitoring and regulation, charting a path distinct from the EU’s heavy‑handed tech oversight.

Anthropic’s International Affairs head Matt Clifford said, "AI is changing the biological risks we face and the way we explore the biosciences. We commend the UK government’s vision in establishing an AI biosecurity lab." Clifford, who previously served as an AI adviser to the British prime minister, stepped down in June last year.

He emphasized that combining top‑tier AI, the UK’s strong research capability and government expertise to detect threats early and accelerate medical solutions will help ensure the safe deployment of AI technologies in industry and society.

Separately, to guard against major vulnerabilities in two widely used technologies that were recently patched after being discovered with AI assistance, the UK government announced a £130 million fund to use AI for identifying cyber weaknesses in critical infrastructure and the economic system, bolstering national cyber‑defence.

In addition, the Sovereign AI Fund will receive a £120 million top‑up, expanding its investment scope to robotics, autonomous systems and advanced manufacturing as well as other physical and industrial AI sectors, and widening its procurement programme for UK start‑ups.

items.title: 成長股、價值股分類大改 標普新規牽動3750億美元資金
items.title_en: Growth and Value Stock Classifications Overhauled; S&P Rule Change Affects $375 B of Funds
paras: 在標普道瓊指數公司（S&P Dow Jones Indices）通過股票分類新規後，成長股與價值股的權重與成分股將迎來全面調整。
根據標普道瓊週五(24日)發布的聲明，該指數提供商將把無形資產、預估盈餘及自由現金流納入指標，用以評估公司股價是否偏向低估。同時，評估公司成長潛力的標準中則將剔除「12個月價格動能」。
新規是在近期徵詢意見後敲定，將於12月21日開盤前的年度成分股調整時生效。
這項變動將促使追蹤相關指數的基金調整持股，以符合新的成分股配置。彭博行業研究分析師James Seyffart估計，至少有3,750億美元的被動型基金追蹤受影響的指數。
標普此次決策之前，市場長期爭論傳統價值衡量指標是否仍然有效。研究人員與基金經理人認為，價值股長期表現低迷，部分原因在於衡量指標存在缺陷，尤其是股價淨值比。
此次調整旨在將研發支出及其他內部開發資產納入考量。依照會計準則，這類支出通常列為費用，而非資產負債表上的資產。批評者指出，這使高度仰賴智慧財產的企業看起來估值偏高，也可能因此被排除在價值股指數之外。
標普並非唯一考慮調整規則的指數編製機構。由於科技巨擘在市場占據主導地位，富時羅素也正重新評估旗下基準指數中，成長股與價值股各占一半的配置方式，相關意見徵詢將於12月11日截止。
paras_en: Following new stock classification rules from S&P Dow Jones Indices, the weightings and constituents of growth and value stocks will undergo a comprehensive adjustment.

According to a statement released by S&P Dow Jones on Friday the 24th, the index provider will incorporate intangible assets, estimated earnings and free cash flow into its metrics to assess whether a company's share price is undervalued. At the same time, the criteria for evaluating a company's growth potential will no longer include the "12‑month price momentum" factor.
The new rules were finalized after a recent public comment period and will take effect at the annual constituent rebalancing before the market opens on December 21.

The change will prompt funds that track the affected indices to adjust their holdings to match the new composition. Bloomberg industry‑research analyst James Seyffart estimates that at least $375 billion of passive funds tracking the impacted indices will need to rebalance.

Before S&P's decision, the market had long debated whether traditional value metrics remain effective. Researchers and fund managers argue that value stocks have underperformed for years, partly because the measurement tools—especially the price‑to‑book ratio—are flawed.

The adjustment aims to bring research and development spending and other internally developed assets into consideration. Under accounting standards, such expenditures are typically recorded as expenses rather than balance‑sheet assets. Critics say this makes companies that rely heavily on intellectual property appear overvalued and could cause them to be excluded from value‑stock indices.

S&P is not the only index compiler contemplating rule changes. Because technology giants dominate the market, FTSE Russell is also re‑examining its benchmark indices' 50/50 split between growth and value stocks, with public comments closing on December 11.

items.title: 半導體設備股災還沒完？花旗示警應材、科林研發、科磊恐再跌3成
items.title_en: Semiconductor Equipment Stock Crash Not Over? Citi Warns Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA Could Fall Another 30%
paras: 投資人擔憂人工智慧(AI)支出熱潮能否持續之際，半導體設備股近期表現不佳，花旗(Citi)警告，科林研發(Lam Research)(LRCX-US)、應用材料(Applied Materials)(AMAT-US)及科磊(KLA)(KLAC-US)近期股價可能才剛開始面臨更大幅度的下跌。
這三家公司都生產晶圓製造設備，用於製造資料中心與AI系統所需的先進晶片，是AI支出熱潮的重要受惠者。然而，隨著市場再度質疑AI交易，投資人擔憂AI產業的債務、以及資料中心建置所需要的龐大支出，半導體設備股也遭到波及。
花旗分析師Atif Malik周四(22日)說：「投資人愈來愈關注潛在的下行情境。」

半導體設備股連續重挫 跌破重要技術指標

科林上周股價下跌逾17%，本周下跌將近13%。該公司周三公布的會計年度第1季財報雖然略優於華爾街預期，表現卻未能滿足投資人對AI相關企業的高度期待。
應材上周股價重挫逾19%，本周再下跌近8%。科磊上周下跌15%後，本周又下跌約12%。
經過這番大幅下跌後，這三檔股票都已跌破50日與200日移動平均線。

花旗估2028年市場受限 基本情境仍有約10%跌幅

Malik指出，目前AI資料中心需求依然強勁，但未來幾年供應短缺可能限制市場成長。花旗根據2028年晶圓製造設備市場的分析認為，這三家公司的股價未來可能進一步大幅下跌。
在花旗對2028年的基本情境預測中，晶圓製造設備市場將受到供應限制。該情境下，應材目標價為335美元、科磊為130美元、科林為208美元，都比目前股價低約10%。
應材周五收盤報每股377.24美元，科磊為145.61美元，科林為230.10美元。
在悲觀情境下，花旗對應材、科磊及科林的目標價分別為259美元、105美元及164美元，意味著三檔股票可能目前價位下跌約30%。
Malik表示，半導體設備需求與這些公司的股價高度相關。資料中心需求前景一旦出現變化，就可能大幅改變這些公司的業務展望。
儘管提出上述下行情境，花旗目前仍給予三家公司「買進」評等。Malik目前對科林、科磊及應材的目標價分別為435美元、290美元及375美元。
paras_en: Investors are worried whether the AI spending boom can continue, and semiconductor equipment stocks have performed poorly recently. Citi warned that Lam Research (LRCX-US), Applied Materials (AMAT-US) and KLA (KLAC-US) may just be starting to face larger declines in their share prices.

All three companies make wafer manufacturing equipment used to produce advanced chips needed for data centers and AI systems, making them key beneficiaries of the AI spending surge. However, as the market again questions AI demand, investors worry about debt in the AI industry and the massive spending required to build data centers, and semiconductor equipment stocks are also being hit.
Citi analyst Atif Malik said on Thursday (the 22nd) that "investors are increasingly focused on potential downside scenarios."

Semiconductor equipment stocks have suffered consecutive heavy losses, breaking through key technical indicators. Lam's stock fell more than 17% last week and is down nearly 13% this week. Although the company's Q1 fiscal year earnings released on Wednesday were slightly better than Wall Street expectations, the performance failed to meet investors' high expectations for AI-related companies.
Applied Materials' stock plunged more than 19% last week and fell another nearly 8% this week. KLA dropped 15% last week and is down about 12% this week.
After these sharp declines, all three stocks have fallen below their 50‑day and 200‑day moving averages.

Citi estimates a roughly 10% downside in the base case scenario for the 2028 market. Malik noted that while AI data‑center demand remains strong, supply shortages in the coming years could limit market growth. Citi’s analysis of the 2028 wafer equipment market suggests the three companies’ shares could fall further.

In Citi’s 2028 base‑case forecast, the wafer equipment market will be constrained by supply. Under this scenario, Applied Materials has a target price of $335, KLA $130 and Lam $208, each about 10% below current levels.
Applied Materials closed Friday at $377.24 per share, KLA at $145.61 and Lam at $230.10.
In a bearish scenario, Citi’s target prices for Applied Materials, KLA and Lam are $259, $105 and $164 respectively, implying the three stocks could be roughly 30% lower than current prices.
Malik said semiconductor equipment demand is closely tied to these companies’ stock prices. A shift in data‑center demand outlook could dramatically alter their business prospects.
Despite outlining these downside scenarios, Citi still rates all three companies as "Buy." Malik’s current target prices are $435 for Lam, $290 for KLA and $375 for Applied Materials.

items.title: 俄美烏11月阿布達比談判！俄首艘柴油油輪赴美、烏克蘭逾900處聚落停電
items.title_en: Russia, U.S., and Ukraine to Hold November Abu Dhabi Talks; Russia Sends First Diesel Tanker to U.S., Over 900 Ukrainian Settlements Lose Power
paras: 俄羅斯與美國、烏克蘭預計11月上半月在阿拉伯聯合大公國首都阿布達比展開三方談判，討論俄烏安全保障問題。俄羅斯總統新聞秘書佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）10月23日表示，目前正討論以三方形式進行談判，未來不排除歐洲參與。
根據陸媒《央視》報導，俄羅斯總統普丁則表示，俄羅斯無意與歐洲開戰。他認為，從歐洲當前的政治進程來看，歐洲人民並不希望與俄羅斯發生戰爭，但部分歐洲國家正全面推動反俄行動，不斷渲染俄羅斯威脅，並開始為與俄羅斯開戰做準備。
普丁強調，俄方的立場也應受到重視。
佩斯科夫同日證實，俄羅斯已派出首艘載運柴油的油輪前往美國，雙方達成的柴油供應協議已開始執行，後續將依計畫持續出貨。
普丁10月21日在聖彼得堡會見美國總統川普特使威特科夫（Steve Witkoff）時表示，俄方已有多艘油輪準備就緒，首艘油輪預計運送4萬噸柴油至美國，後續船隻也將陸續出發。他並指出，俄羅斯也有能力向美國市場供應大量化肥。
俄羅斯副總理諾瓦克（Alexander Novak）21日表示，俄美柴油供應合約已進入簽署最後階段，首艘油輪預計22日啟程。他預期，俄羅斯有望在2026年底前向美國以外的其他國家供應柴油，並可能全面恢復柴油出口規模。
俄羅斯政府10日宣布，部分解除柴油出口禁令，允許現階段向全球市場供應50萬噸柴油，俄羅斯石油公司將在政府協調下與外國交易方簽訂供應合約。
普丁指出，他與川普多次通話時均強調，必須盡快結束俄烏衝突，因為戰事不僅造成軍人傷亡，也波及平民。

烏克蘭能源設施遭襲　逾900處聚落停電

俄烏戰事持續之際，烏克蘭敖德薩州與日托米爾州官員表示，當地能源及民用設施在22日晚間至23日凌晨遭俄軍攻擊。
敖德薩州軍事行政長官基佩爾（Oleh Kiper）23日表示，俄軍攻擊能源企業DTEK在當地的能源設施及民用設施。
DTEK指出，旗下的一座熱電廠遭大規模攻擊，設備嚴重受損，目前已停止發電。該公司並表示，自俄烏戰爭爆發以來，旗下發電廠累計遭到逾230次攻擊。
日托米爾州軍事行政長官布涅奇科（Vitalii Bunechko）則表示，當地能源設施同樣遭到襲擊。截至23日上午7時，當地仍有逾900個居民點停電，關鍵基礎設施則依靠備用電源維持運作。
俄羅斯國防部23日表示，俄軍當天凌晨以無人機攻擊烏克蘭多處目標，包括敖德薩州一艘據稱正替烏軍運送物資的貨船，以及維爾科沃港的無人艇停泊區、存放地點與相關設施。此外，俄軍也以無人機攻擊波爾塔瓦州一處用於存放及維修軍事裝備的鐵路貨場。
paras_en: Russia, the United States and Ukraine are expected to hold three‑way talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, in the first half of November to discuss security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine. Russian President’s press secretary Dmitry Peskov said on Oct. 23 that a trilateral format is being considered and that European participation is not ruled out for the future.

According to Chinese state media CCTV, President Vladimir Putin said Russia has no intention of going to war with Europe. He believes that, given the current political trajectory in Europe, European peoples do not want a war with Russia, but some European countries are pushing a full‑scale anti‑Russia campaign, constantly portraying Russia as a threat and beginning to prepare for war against Moscow.
Putin stressed that Russia’s position must also be taken seriously.

Peskov confirmed on the same day that Russia has dispatched its first diesel‑carrying tanker to the United States, and the diesel supply agreement reached by the two sides has already been put into effect, with further shipments planned to continue as scheduled.

During a meeting in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21, Putin told U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff that several Russian tankers are ready, with the first expected to deliver 40,000 tonnes of diesel to the United States, and additional vessels to follow. He also noted that Russia is capable of supplying large quantities of fertilizer to the U.S. market.

Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on the 21st that the Russia‑U.S. diesel supply contract is in its final signing stage and that the first tanker is slated to depart on the 22nd. He expects Russia to be able to supply diesel to countries beyond the United States by the end of 2026 and to potentially restore its full export capacity.

The Russian government announced on the 10th that it is partially lifting the diesel export ban, allowing up to 500,000 tonnes of diesel to be supplied to the global market at present, with Rosneft signing supply contracts with foreign counterparties under government coordination.

Putin pointed out that in his multiple phone calls with President Trump he repeatedly emphasized the need to end the Russia‑Ukraine conflict as quickly as possible, because the war not only causes military casualties but also affects civilians.

Ukrainian energy facilities were attacked, leaving more than 900 settlements without power. Amid the ongoing war, officials in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zhytomyr regions said that local energy and civilian infrastructure were hit by Russian attacks from the night of the 22nd to the early hours of the 23rd.
Odesa regional military administration head Oleh Kiper said on the 23rd that Russian forces struck energy facilities owned by DTEK as well as civilian infrastructure in the region.

DTEK reported that one of its combined‑heat‑and‑power plants suffered a massive attack, with severe equipment damage that forced the plant to stop generating electricity. The company added that since the war began, its power plants have been hit more than 230 times.

Zhytomyr regional military administration head Vitalii Bunechko said that local energy facilities were also attacked. As of 7 a.m. on the 23rd, more than 900 residential settlements remained without electricity, while critical infrastructure continued to operate on backup power.

The Russian Defense Ministry said on the 23rd that Russian forces used drones in the early morning to strike multiple Ukrainian targets, including a cargo ship in Odesa allegedly transporting supplies for Ukrainian troops, the unmanned‑boat mooring area, storage sites and related facilities at the Vylkove port, and a railway freight depot in Poltava used for storing and repairing military equipment.

items.title: AI代理竟能突破沙箱、繞過防火牆 OpenAI揭露多項內部漏洞 訓練暫停11天後重啟
items.title_en: AI Agents Can Break Out of Sandboxes and Bypass Firewalls: OpenAI Discloses Multiple Internal Vulnerabilities, Resumes Training After 11-Day Pause
paras: OpenAI周五(23日)披露，一個內部AI研究模型曾在訓練期間利用網路系統的設定錯誤，取得有限的公開網路存取能力。公司因此暫停最先進模型的訓練與測試，展開大規模安全檢查與漏洞修補，約11天後於10月1日恢復強化學習訓練及內部推論工作。OpenAI並宣布，在安全防護能力進一步提升前，前沿模型訓練將禁止直接連接公開網際網路。
這起事件發生於9月20日，當時仍在訓練中的內部研究模型，利用DNS解析器的設定錯誤，短暫取得有限的外部網路存取能力。OpenAI表示，事件已受到控制，但也暴露出訓練環境的防護缺口，因此決定暫停最強模型的訓練與評估，重新檢查虛擬機器隔離、網路限制、監控系統及內部服務的安全性。公司未公布此次訓練中斷造成的財務影響。
OpenAI指出，隨著前沿模型的能力持續提升，安全挑戰已不再只是讓模型遵守指令，而是確保模型無法利用軟體漏洞、錯誤設定或系統間的連線，突破原本設計的操作範圍。AI連接網路有助於學習搜尋資料、瀏覽網頁及操作網路應用程式，但如果模型尚未完成安全訓練與對齊程序，未經授權的網路存取便可能讓它接觸外部系統，增加潛在風險。
為降低風險，OpenAI決定讓最先進模型在訓練期間維持離線，不再直接接觸真正的公開網際網路。公司建立名為「離線世界」的訓練環境，預先將大量網頁內容收錄、索引及快取於內部系統，讓模型能在不直接連網的情況下練習搜尋、瀏覽及操作網頁應用程式。目前所有前沿模型的強化學習訓練，都採用這種離線互動模式。
不過，OpenAI並未將整套訓練設施完全切斷外部網路。由於實驗執行、監控、日誌記錄及身分驗證等工作仍需要部分連線，公司改以多層防禦限制風險，包括虛擬機器、受限制的容器、網路流量控管、防火牆、雲端安全邊界、身分與存取管理，以及私人網路等措施，避免模型透過其他服務或間接管道繞過限制。
在程式執行與電腦操作方面，OpenAI利用Linux環境中的輕量級虛擬機器及受限制容器隔離AI代理與底層主機，並針對macOS及Windows採用虛擬化環境；需要加速運算的工作，則使用GPU容器與使用者空間沙箱。公司也設置活動監控與自動暫停機制，當系統出現異常行為時，可及時停止實驗，降低漏洞被進一步利用的風險。
為驗證防護措施是否有效，OpenAI採取「用AI找AI系統漏洞」的方式，讓高能力模型組成紅隊測試團隊，在專門隔離的研究環境中嘗試突破安全限制。公司投入數千億個token進行測試，要求模型嘗試連接公開網際網路、跨越內部安全邊界，以及與原本應該隔離的其他AI代理交換資訊。

參與測試的模型包括即將推出的GPT-6 Astra Cyber，以及一款內部前沿模型。OpenAI向測試代理提供基礎設施原始碼、設定細節及潛在漏洞相關文件，讓它們能以更接近真實攻擊者的條件尋找弱點。部分測試更假設代理已經逃離沙箱、避開監控並取得主機控制權，再檢查外圍網路與雲端防護能否阻止其連接外部網路。測試在專門隔離的基礎設施副本中進行，並由監控與自動停止機制把關，雲端合作夥伴也協助監督實驗及處理發現的問題。
OpenAI表示，測試代理成功找出多項先前未知的開源軟體漏洞，以及公司內部服務的設定錯誤。部分缺陷可能讓代理逃離沙箱、在系統間移動、取得有限的外部網路存取能力，或跨越原本用來隔離不同代理的安全邊界。隨著測試持續進行，模型找到的漏洞與設定錯誤數量明顯下降，但公司警告，未來能力更強的模型仍可能發現目前尚未掌握的弱點。

在虛擬機器安全方面，紅隊代理將多個漏洞串聯，嘗試突破虛擬機器隔離並在底層主機執行程式碼。OpenAI已建立自動化流程，協助分類、排除重複漏洞及驗證修補結果，並針對受影響的開源專案提交修正，涉及Kata Containers、gVisor及Moby/Docker等元件。公司也列出CVE-2026-24834、CVE-2026-74753、CVE-2026-80521及CVE-2026-80841等相關修補工作，另有部分漏洞已通報，但尚未公開細節。

在網路隔離方面，OpenAI發現，即使大幅縮減訓練環境可使用的連網管道，仍有部分負責指標監測、日誌記錄及身分驗證管理的服務保留必要連線。測試代理利用這些服務的漏洞或特殊功能組合，找到取得有限外部網路存取的途徑。例如，在假設主機已遭入侵的情境中，代理利用防火牆允許的連線接觸原本受限制的驗證端點，再讓該端點取得由模型提供的網址。其他測試也發現，DNS與防火牆設定錯誤，以及服務代為擷取外部網址的功能，都可能形成繞過限制的路徑。
測試還發現，即使AI代理沒有直接網路連線，也可能利用共享硬體或服務形成隱蔽通訊管道。在一項實驗中，分別執行於不同虛擬機器的代理，在無法使用網路或共享可寫入檔案的情況下，仍利用處理器快取的存取時間差傳遞訊息。一個代理透過清除特定快取資料編碼資訊，另一個代理則測量重新讀取資料所需的時間，藉由快取命中與未命中的速度差異還原訊息。這類快取時序技術過去也曾出現在Spectre與Meltdown攻擊中。
其他測試則發現，共享儲存空間、同一執行容器中的CPU資源競爭，以及離線網頁基礎設施中的TLS憑證快取，都可能被利用來傳遞資訊。OpenAI表示，這些通道的傳輸速度通常較慢，利用難度也較高，但仍可能破壞原本預期的代理隔離，因此公司已在監控系統中加入相關偵測機制。
此次測試也揭露廣泛使用的資料壓縮工具Brotli存在安全問題。OpenAI表示，攻擊者可能透過傳送惡意資料，讓受影響系統執行攻擊者提供的程式碼，相關影響範圍包括使用Node.js、Bun及Envoy等常見網路軟體的環境。Brotli原始碼中的根本原因雖已於2月修正，但當時尚未被認定為安全漏洞，因此未立即發布新版本；在OpenAI揭露問題後，Brotli已發布更新版本並公開相關漏洞紀錄。
外部安全評估機構也提出相關疑慮。AI安全評估機構METR與Redwood Research於10月22日表示，在今年稍早進行的一項試點審查中，發現OpenAI內部系統存在數項新漏洞，其中一種利用方式可能讓AI代理將數百次行動隱藏在監控之外。OpenAI告訴這些機構，所有影響正式環境防護措施的漏洞均已修補，但METR與Redwood Research表示，尚未自行驗證修補是否有效。
自7月發生Hugging Face相關事件後，OpenAI也持續檢視AI模型的活動，並已向超過100個組織通報與AI代理未經授權活動相關的事件。這顯示，隨著AI代理逐漸具備更強的程式設計與資安能力，企業面臨的風險不再只限於模型本身是否遵守指令，也包括模型能否利用基礎設施缺陷，突破原本設計的安全限制。
OpenAI表示，在完成紅隊測試、修補已知弱點並改善監控與自動停止機制後，公司判定目前的防護措施足以恢復前沿模型的強化學習訓練及內部推論。訓練工作於10月1日恢復，距離暫停約11天。接下來，公司將持續改善虛擬機器安全、與雲端合作夥伴共同測試外圍防護、掃描程式碼與雲端設定、驗證監控及自動暫停機制，並將高算力紅隊測試納入未來前沿模型訓練與評估的安全審查程序。
OpenAI強調，安全防護並非完成一次測試就能一勞永逸。隨著模型能力進一步提升，公司將持續投入算力尋找沙箱、運算叢集及周邊系統的弱點，並在對外發布模型前進行安全與對齊評估，再為正式產品部署相應防護措施。
paras_en: OpenAI disclosed on Friday (the 23rd) that an internal AI research model had, during training, exploited a misconfiguration in the network system to gain limited public internet access. The company therefore halted training and testing of its most advanced models, launched a large‑scale security audit and patching effort, and about 11 days later, on October 1, resumed reinforcement‑learning training and internal inference work. OpenAI also announced that, until its protective capabilities are further improved, frontier‑model training will be prohibited from connecting directly to the public internet.

The incident occurred on September 20, when a research model still in training used a DNS resolver misconfiguration to briefly obtain limited external network access. OpenAI said the incident was contained but exposed a protection gap in the training environment, prompting a pause in training and evaluation of its strongest models and a re‑examination of VM isolation, network restrictions, monitoring systems, and internal service security. The company did not disclose the financial impact of the training interruption.

OpenAI noted that as frontier models become more capable, the security challenge is no longer just getting models to follow instructions, but ensuring they cannot exploit software bugs, misconfigurations, or inter‑system connections to break out of their intended operating bounds. Network connectivity helps models learn to search for information, browse web pages, and operate web applications, but if a model has not completed safety training and alignment, unauthorized network access could expose it to external systems and increase potential risk.

To reduce risk, OpenAI decided to keep its most advanced models offline during training, removing direct contact with the real public internet. The company built a "offline world" training environment that pre‑loads, indexes, and caches large amounts of web content inside its internal systems, allowing models to practice searching, browsing, and interacting with web applications without a live connection. All reinforcement‑learning training for frontier models now uses this offline interaction mode.

However, OpenAI did not completely cut off the training infrastructure from external networks. Because experiment execution, monitoring, logging, and authentication still require some connectivity, the company implemented multiple layers of defense to limit risk, including virtual machines, restricted containers, network traffic controls, firewalls, cloud security perimeters, identity and access management, and private networks, to prevent models from bypassing limits via other services or indirect channels.

For program execution and computer operations, OpenAI isolates AI agents from the host OS using lightweight VMs and restricted containers in a Linux environment, and employs virtualization for macOS and Windows; GPU containers and user‑space sandboxes are used for compute‑intensive tasks. The company also set up activity monitoring and automatic pause mechanisms that can halt experiments promptly when abnormal behavior is detected, reducing the chance of further exploitation of any vulnerability.

To verify the effectiveness of its safeguards, OpenAI adopted a "use AI to find AI system bugs" approach, forming a red‑team of high‑capacity models that attempted to breach security limits in a specially isolated research environment. The company invested billions of tokens in testing, tasking the models with trying to connect to the public internet, cross internal security boundaries, and exchange information with other AI agents that should have been isolated.

Models participating in the tests included the upcoming GPT‑6 Astra Cyber and another internal frontier model. OpenAI provided the test agents with infrastructure source code, configuration details, and documents on potential vulnerabilities, enabling them to search for weaknesses under conditions closer to real attackers. Some tests assumed the agents had already escaped the sandbox, evaded monitoring, and gained host control, then examined whether peripheral network and cloud defenses could block external connections. The tests were run on isolated copies of the infrastructure, overseen by monitoring and automatic stop mechanisms, with cloud partners assisting in supervision and issue handling.

OpenAI reported that the test agents uncovered several previously unknown open‑source software vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in internal services. Some flaws could allow agents to escape the sandbox, move laterally across systems, obtain limited external network access, or cross security boundaries meant to isolate different agents. As testing progressed, the number of discovered bugs and misconfigurations declined markedly, but the company warned that more capable future models could still find weaknesses that are not yet understood.

In the VM security domain, red‑team agents chained multiple vulnerabilities to try breaking VM isolation and executing code on the host. OpenAI has built automated workflows to classify, de‑duplicate, and verify patches, and it has submitted fixes to affected open‑source projects, including components such as Kata Containers, gVisor, and Moby/Docker. The company listed related remediation work for CVE‑2026‑24834, CVE‑2026‑74753, CVE‑2026‑80521, and CVE‑2026‑80841; some vulnerabilities have been reported but details have not yet been made public.

Regarding network isolation, OpenAI found that even after drastically reducing the training environment’s available network pathways, certain services needed for metric monitoring, logging, and identity management retained necessary connections. Test agents leveraged bugs or special feature combinations in these services to obtain limited external network access. For example, in a scenario where the host was assumed compromised, an agent used a firewall‑allowed connection to reach a previously restricted authentication endpoint, which then fetched a URL supplied by the model. Other tests discovered that DNS and firewall misconfigurations, as well as services that fetch external URLs on behalf of others, could form bypass routes.

The tests also showed that even without direct network links, AI agents could create covert communication channels via shared hardware or services. In one experiment, agents running on separate VMs, unable to use the network or share writable files, still exchanged messages by exploiting timing differences in processor cache access. One agent cleared specific cache lines to encode information, while the other measured the time to reload the data, reconstructing the message from cache‑hit versus miss latency—a technique reminiscent of Spectre and Meltdown attacks.

Other findings indicated that shared storage, CPU resource contention within the same container, and TLS‑certificate caching in the offline‑web infrastructure could also be abused for data transfer. OpenAI said these channels are generally slower and harder to exploit, but they can still undermine the intended isolation of agents, so the company has added detection mechanisms for such activity to its monitoring systems.

The testing also uncovered security issues in the widely used data‑compression tool Brotli. OpenAI warned that attackers could send malicious data that causes vulnerable systems to execute attacker‑provided code, affecting environments that use Node.js, Bun, Envoy, and other common networking software. Although the root cause in Brotli’s source code was fixed in February, it was not classified as a security bug at the time, so no immediate release was issued. After OpenAI’s disclosure, Brotli released an updated version and published the related vulnerability record.

External security assessment firms also raised concerns. AI safety assessors METR and Redwood Research said on October 22 that a pilot review earlier this year found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s internal systems, one of which could let an AI agent hide hundreds of actions from monitoring. OpenAI told the firms that all vulnerabilities affecting production‑environment protections have been patched, but METR and Redwood noted they have not independently verified the effectiveness of those patches.

Since the Hugging Face incident in July, OpenAI has continuously reviewed AI model activity and has reported unauthorized agent activity to more than 100 organizations. This shows that as AI agents gain stronger programming and cybersecurity capabilities, the risk to enterprises extends beyond whether a model follows instructions to whether it can exploit infrastructure flaws and break designed security boundaries.

OpenAI stated that after completing the red‑team tests, patching known weaknesses, and improving monitoring and automatic pause mechanisms, it deemed its current protections sufficient to resume reinforcement‑learning training and internal inference for frontier models. Training resumed on October 1, roughly 11 days after the pause. Going forward, the company will keep enhancing VM security, jointly test peripheral defenses with cloud partners, scan code and cloud configurations, verify monitoring and auto‑pause mechanisms, and incorporate high‑compute red‑team testing into future frontier‑model training and safety review processes.

OpenAI emphasized that security is not a one‑time effort. As model capabilities continue to grow, the company will keep investing compute power to hunt for sandbox, cluster, and peripheral system weaknesses, conduct safety and alignment assessments before releasing models externally, and deploy appropriate protections for production products.

items.title: 輝達分析師示警：2027年規劃中AI資料中心容量恐有45%無法建成
items.title_en: Nvidia Analyst Warns 45% of Planned AI Data Center Capacity for 2027 May Remain Unbuilt
paras: 華爾街一名看空分析師警告，明年規劃中的AI資料中心容量可能有近一半無法建成，恐威脅輝達(NVDA-US)晶片的未來需求。
據《巴隆周刊》週五(23日)報導，Seaport Research Partners分析師Jay Goldberg估計，2027年已宣布的55GW資料中心容量中，最終只有30GW能夠實現，意味著可能出現45%的缺口。
Goldberg維持「賣出」評級，目標價為180美元，較週四收盤價低約15%。
他指出，電工人力短缺、燃氣渦輪機供應不足，以及電力併網問題，是阻礙資料中心建設的主要因素。
微軟(MSFT-US)近期退出一項由輝達支持、位於英格蘭的Nscale資料中心計畫，因該設施原定取得的電力連接時間延後至2030年代。這座資料中心原本計劃容納超過2.3萬顆輝達GPU。
亞馬遜(AMZN-US)也面臨類似問題。由於等待資料中心取得足夠電力以投入運作，部分輝達伺服器目前仍閒置在倉庫中。
輝達面臨的財務風險
Goldberg的疑慮不僅在於建設延誤。輝達也正協助部分預期將採購其晶片的公司取得資金。
他認為，投資、貸款與信用保證相當於「另一種形式的折價」，讓輝達無須正式調降晶片價格，也能藉此支撐銷售。
Goldberg認為，相較於仰賴三家實力雄厚的科技巨頭，輝達更希望擁有200家規模較小、且依賴輝達的客戶。
然而，CoreWeave(CRWV-US)與Nebius(NBIS-US)等規模較小的雲端服務商，需要大量融資才能持續採購輝達晶片。如果這些公司陷入困境，輝達可能面臨銷售減弱及利潤率承壓的風險。
截至7月26日，輝達的供應與產能承諾金額達2,790億美元，是前一季公布的1,190億美元的兩倍以上。
輝達也揭露，對採購其硬體的服務供應商，另有360億美元的雲端服務承諾。
輝達在最新一季財報文件中警告，基礎建設短缺可能延後晶片採購，進而損害營收。部分供應承諾則可以調整或取消。
分析師對資料中心建設前景看法不一
研究機構SemiAnalysis的看法較為樂觀。該機構指出，目前有40座園區、總容量超過24GW的資料中心，已進入建設進度較為成熟的階段。
該機構研究人員週一寫道，「大型基地確實正在興建，而且許多工程都按進度進行。」
資料中心延後完工，也不代表輝達一定會失去相關晶片銷售。這些晶片仍可能轉售給已具備足夠電力的客戶。
Goldberg本人也預期，輝達的銷售額將在2027年初之前創下新高，但他認為，接下來一年相關風險將逐漸升高。
在Polymarket上，輝達於2026年底成為全球市值最高公司的機率，本月稍早曾高於80%，但據週五上午數據，已降至56%，蘋果(AAPL-US)的機率則升至41%。
paras_en: A bearish Wall Street analyst warned that nearly half of the AI data center capacity planned for next year may not be built, threatening future demand for Nvidia (NVDA-US) chips.

According to Barron's on Friday the 23rd, Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg estimates that of the 55GW of data center capacity announced for 2027, only 30GW will actually materialize, implying a 45% shortfall.
Goldberg maintains a "sell" rating with a target price of $180, about 15% below Thursday's closing price.
He points to a shortage of electricians, insufficient gas turbine supply, and power‑grid interconnection issues as the main obstacles to data‑center construction.

Microsoft (MSFT-US) recently withdrew from an Nvidia‑backed Nscale data‑center project in England after the facility’s power‑connection timeline was pushed back into the 2030s. The center had been slated to house more than 23,000 Nvidia GPUs.
Amazon (AMZN-US) faces a similar problem. While waiting for sufficient power to bring its data center online, some Nvidia servers remain idle in warehouses.
Financial risks facing Nvidia
Goldberg’s concerns go beyond construction delays. Nvidia is also helping some of the companies expected to buy its chips secure financing.
He argues that investments, loans and credit guarantees amount to a "different form of discount," allowing Nvidia to support sales without formally cutting chip prices.
Goldberg believes that rather than relying on three large tech giants, Nvidia prefers to have about 200 smaller customers that depend on its chips.

However, smaller cloud providers such as CoreWeave (CRWV-US) and Nebius (NBIS-US) need substantial financing to keep buying Nvidia chips. If these firms run into trouble, Nvidia could see weaker sales and pressured margins.
As of July 26, Nvidia's supply and capacity commitment amount reached $279 billion, more than double the $119 billion disclosed in the prior quarter.
Nvidia also disclosed an additional $36 billion of cloud‑service commitments from providers purchasing its hardware.
In its latest quarterly filing, Nvidia warned that infrastructure shortages could delay chip purchases and hurt revenue, and that some supply commitments may be adjusted or cancelled.
Analysts are divided on the outlook for data‑center construction
Research firm SemiAnalysis is more optimistic, noting that 40 sites with a combined capacity of over 24GW are now in relatively mature construction phases.
The firm’s researchers wrote on Monday, "Large campuses are indeed being built, and many projects are on schedule."
Delays in data‑center completion do not necessarily mean Nvidia will lose those chip sales; the chips could be resold to customers with sufficient power.
Goldberg himself expects Nvidia’s sales to hit a new peak before early 2027, but he sees the related risk rising over the next year.

On Polymarket, the probability that Nvidia will be the world’s most valuable company by the end of 2026 was above 80% earlier this month, but Friday morning data showed it had fallen to 56%, while Apple (AAPL-US) rose to 41%.

items.title: AI需求爆棚卻缺錢！黃仁勳：資金需求遠超供給 新型雲端業者融資受考驗
items.title_en: AI Demand Booms but Money Is Short! Jensen Huang: Funding Needs Far Outstrip Supply, New Cloud Providers Face Financing Test
paras: 《CNBC》週五 (23 日) 報導，輝達 (NVDA-US) 柏林 GTC 大會展現人工智慧 (AI) 基礎建設的龐大商機，但場邊討論也浮現另一層隱憂：隨著業者大舉借貸擴建，資金供給能否跟上投資需求，正成為產業關注焦點。輝達執行長黃仁勳直言，市場對資金的需求遠高於目前可取得的規模。
柏林 GTC 是黃仁勳為期約一週半歐洲行的重要壓軸。他 21 日在行程中會晤多國領袖、發表新產品，也在台上與小型機器鴨互動。不過，熱鬧的展示之外，與會的 AI 基礎建設業者、投資人及資料中心供應商，談論的重點包括新型雲端業者的財務壓力、小型資料中心部署，以及資金取得難度。
大會最後一天，提供 AI 算力租賃服務的新型雲端業者 (neocloud) 股價再遭重挫。
CoreWeave (CRWV-US) 週四 (22日) 收跌約 10%，Nebius (NBIS-US) 下跌約 7%，延續近期因高額借貸引發疑慮的震盪走勢。
一名 AI 基礎建設公司主管表示，大量尚無信用評等的企業投入這個市場，正讓投資人感到不安。
黃仁勳對需求前景仍抱持樂觀看法。他表示，從基本面來看，市場對新型雲端業者的需求極為強勁。不過，輝達也持有多家相關公司的股權，是這波算力擴張的重要參與者。
如何加快算力上線，是這次大會的另一項主軸。
黃仁勳發表DSX POD，將Vera Rubin運算系統、網路、供電與液冷設備預先整合於模組化貨櫃，將7座Vera Rubin AI機櫃裝進一個貨櫃，並在工廠完成組裝與測試後出貨，並可透過一般道路運輸，藉此縮短部署時間，最快可於 14天 內完成部署並投入運作。
黃仁勳指出，資料中心延後啟用，可能造成數十億美元營收損失。若能將更多整合工作提前移至供應鏈完成，就有望加快設施上線速度。
大型算力需求者也開始尋找較小規模的部署機會。 9 月媒體引述消息人士報導，OpenAI 與 Anthropic 正洽尋較小型的 AI 資料中心交易，以取得所需算力。
然而，加快部署仍須龐大資金支撐。高盛估計，2026 年至 2031 年間，涵蓋運算、資料中心與電力的 AI 相關資本支出，合計可能達約 7.6 兆美元。黃仁勳則在週三的大會上表示，一座 1 吉瓦 (GW) 資料中心的建置成本約為 500 億美元。
黃仁勳週四接受訪問時指出，目前缺少的是支撐成長所需的營運資金。由於 AI 各領域同時出現龐大需求，資金供給因此吃緊。
「資金需求遠大於可取得的資金。」黃仁勳表示，但他也相信，這個問題最終會獲得解決。
一名 AI 基礎建設融資公司的主管表示，資金很快就會成為產業發展的瓶頸。隨著算力需求持續擴張，業者除了設法取得晶片、電力與機房，也必須證明自己有能力籌措並承擔建設所需的資金。
paras_en: CNBC reported on Friday (the 23rd) that Nvidia's (NVDA-US) GTC conference in Berlin showcased the massive business opportunity in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, but side‑stage discussions also revealed another concern: as companies borrow heavily to expand, can capital supply keep up with investment demand, which is becoming a focal point for the industry. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said outright that the market's demand for funding far exceeds the amount currently available.

The Berlin GTC is the centerpiece of Jensen Huang's roughly week‑and‑a‑half European tour. On the 21st he met multiple national leaders, unveiled new products, and even interacted onstage with a small robot duck. Beyond the lively demos, AI infrastructure firms, investors and data‑center suppliers at the event focused on the financial pressure on new‑type cloud providers, the deployment of small data centers, and the difficulty of securing capital.
On the final day of the conference, the stock of a new‑type cloud provider offering AI compute‑rental services (neocloud) tumbled again.
CoreWeave (CRWV-US) fell about 10% on Thursday (the 22nd) and Nebius (NBIS-US) dropped roughly 7%, continuing the recent volatility sparked by concerns over large‑scale borrowing.
An executive at an AI infrastructure company said that a flood of firms without credit ratings entering the market is unsettling investors.

Jensen Huang remains optimistic about demand prospects. He said that fundamentally, demand for new‑type cloud providers is extremely strong. Nvidia also holds equity stakes in several related companies, making it a key participant in this wave of compute expansion.
Accelerating the rollout of compute capacity was another key theme of the conference.

Jensen Huang unveiled the DSX POD, which pre‑integrates the Vera Rubin computing system, networking, power and liquid‑cooling equipment into a modular container. Seven Vera Rubin AI cabinets are packed into a single container, assembled and tested at the factory, then shipped and road‑transportable, shortening deployment time to as fast as 14 days from shipment to operation.

Huang noted that delayed data‑center activation could cost tens of billions of dollars in revenue. If more integration work is shifted upstream to the supply chain, facility rollout speed could be accelerated.

Large compute users are also looking for smaller‑scale deployment opportunities. Media reports in September quoted sources saying OpenAI and Anthropic are negotiating for smaller AI data‑center deals to secure the needed compute.

However, faster deployment still requires massive capital. Goldman Sachs estimates AI‑related capital expenditures—including compute, data centers and power—could total about $7.6 trillion between 2026 and 2031. Huang said at Wednesday’s event that building a 1‑gigawatt data center costs roughly $50 billion.
In an interview on Thursday, Huang said the current shortage is operating capital needed to support growth. With huge demand across AI sectors, funding is becoming tight.
"Funding demand far exceeds the capital that can be obtained," Huang said, but he believes the issue will eventually be resolved.

An executive at an AI infrastructure financing firm warned that capital will soon become a bottleneck for industry development. As compute demand keeps expanding, companies must not only secure chips, power and facilities, but also demonstrate they can raise and bear the financing required for construction.

items.title: 偶遇馬雲成轉折 黑石豪押AI全產業鏈
items.title_en: A Chance Encounter with Jack Ma Marks a Turning Point as Blackstone Makes a Massive Bet on the AI Industry Chain
paras: 黑石集團（Blackstone）執行長蘇世民（Steve Schwarzman）透露，公司如今大舉押注人工智慧（AI），源於十多年前一次與阿里巴巴創辦人馬雲的偶然相遇。
蘇世民接受彭博電視台「Leaders With Francine Lacqua」節目採訪時回憶，2015年，他在中國搭乘客運時，恰好坐在馬雲旁邊。馬雲當時主動談起AI，但蘇世民坦言：「說實話，我當時完全不知道他在講什麼。」
馬雲向他解釋，AI將是影響最深遠的技術變革，並改變整個世界。這場交談後來成為黑石調整投資方向的重要契機。
如今，這家管理約1.3兆美元資產的另類投資巨頭，已將AI布局延伸至資料中心、能源、晶片融資、企業股權及投資決策等多個領域。
黑石管理的資料中心資產規模約達2,000億美元，並與Google(GOOGL-US)合作開展雲端運算業務。公司也持有OpenAI等AI實驗室的股份，並以博通(AVGO-US)和輝達(NVDA-US)的晶片為基礎開展融資業務。
除了運算基礎設施與晶片，黑石也投資發電廠及資料中心散熱設備，布局支撐AI運算所需的關鍵環節。
在企業應用方面，黑石透過旗下數百家企業推廣AI技術，相關工作主要由Ode負責。Ode是一家企業諮詢公司，由黑石與Anthropic、私募股權公司Hellman & Friedman及其他投資者合作創立。
AI也進入黑石內部的投資流程。AI模型如今已參與評估潛在投資項目，成為分析交易的工具之一。
從基礎設施到企業應用，黑石試圖從AI產業鏈的不同環節尋找投資機會，但布局越廣，也意味著風險可能跨越多種資產類別。
資料中心擴張遇阻 AI投資風險升溫
身為美國規模最大的商業資料中心業主，黑石正面臨日益升高的政治與社會壓力。
隨著外界對工作機會流失、AI失控風險及資料中心高耗電問題的擔憂加深，相關建設遭遇更多反對聲浪，黑石部分項目也受到阻礙。
資本市場的疑慮則集中在AI支出能否持續。隨著黑石、阿波羅全球管理公司、Brookfield Asset Management及KKR等大型資產管理業者持續加碼AI，投資者可能在股票、信貸及基礎設施等不同資產中，反覆承擔相同的AI投資風險。
一旦AI投資週期逆轉，衝擊可能同時傳導至多個市場。換言之，布局多個產業環節，不代表就能真正分散風險。
蘇世民：重大技術變革需數十年才能兌現價值
面對AI投資可能過熱的疑慮，蘇世民認為，重大技術創新往往需要數十年才能充分展現經濟價值，初期投入不一定能迅速轉化為利潤。
他以電力基礎設施為例指出，愛迪生於1882年發明電燈泡，但要讓電燈泡真正發揮作用，仍需要建設完整的電網，而這個過程花了約40年。
蘇世民表示，「當時還沒有人了解廣播，也沒有人了解電視。建設電網時，沒有人會想到這些應用。」
電網最初是為電燈泡等用途而建設，後來卻成為廣播、電視等新興產業發展的基礎。蘇世民認為，AI目前也處於發展早期，未來的應用範圍與商業價值仍可能持續擴大。
他表示，「而我們現在還處於這一進程的早期階段。」
這也是黑石長期投資AI基礎設施的核心思路：即使部分項目短期回報有限，底層設施仍可能隨技術發展而產生更廣泛的價值。不過，長期前景並不保證每項投資都能獲利，資本支出、能源成本與實際需求之間的平衡，仍是投資者必須面對的考驗。
談美國政治極化 蘇世民籲回到中間地帶
採訪中，蘇世民也談及美國日益加劇的政治分歧。身為長期共和黨支持者，他表示，不同政治陣營之間的距離越來越遠，跨陣營溝通也變得更加困難。
他談到，「我認為，如今無論身處哪個政黨都不容易。過去，社會中間地帶曾經相當廣闊，而我就屬於這一部分。」
他接著表示，「如今，我們已經走到了人們不再願意傾聽彼此的地步。我認為這非常令人遺憾，也給整個國家帶來了挑戰。我們需要重新回到一個更加平衡的中間地帶。」
從與馬雲的一次偶遇，到如今橫跨資料中心、雲端運算、晶片融資及能源基礎設施的投資布局，黑石的AI策略已遠遠超出單純投資科技股的範疇。
蘇世民押注AI的長期潛力，但隨著資料中心建設阻力增加、資本支出持續攀升，以及市場對投資集中風險的疑慮升溫，黑石仍須證明，對AI產業鏈的全面布局能否轉化為持續且合理的投資回報。
paras_en: Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman disclosed that the firm’s current large‑scale bet on artificial intelligence (AI) stems from a chance encounter with Alibaba founder Jack Ma more than a decade ago.

Schwarzman recalled on Bloomberg Television’s “Leaders With Francine Lacqua” that in 2015, while riding a bus in China, he happened to sit next to Jack Ma. Ma proactively brought up AI, but Schwarzman admitted, “To be honest, I had no idea what he was talking about at the time.”

Ma explained that AI would be the most far‑reaching technological transformation and would change the entire world. That conversation later became a key catalyst for Blackstone to adjust its investment direction.

Today, the alternative‑investment giant that manages roughly $1.3 trillion in assets has extended its AI footprint into data centers, energy, chip financing, corporate equity and investment‑decision processes among other areas.

Blackstone’s data‑center assets total about $200 billion and it partners with Google (GOOGL‑US) on cloud‑computing services. The firm also holds stakes in AI labs such as OpenAI and conducts financing activities based on chips from Broadcom (AVGO‑US) and Nvidia (NVDA‑US).
Beyond compute infrastructure and chips, Blackstone is investing in power plants and data‑center cooling equipment, positioning itself in the critical links needed to support AI workloads.

On the enterprise‑application side, Blackstone promotes AI technology through hundreds of portfolio companies, with the work largely handled by Ode. Ode is a consulting firm co‑founded by Blackstone, Anthropic, private‑equity firm Hellman & Friedman and other investors.
AI has also entered Blackstone’s internal investment process. AI models now participate in evaluating potential deals, becoming one of the tools used to analyze transactions.

From infrastructure to enterprise applications, Blackstone is seeking investment opportunities across different segments of the AI value chain, but the broader the exposure, the more the risk can span multiple asset classes.
Data‑center expansion faces headwinds, raising AI‑investment risk
As the United States’ largest commercial data‑center owner, Blackstone is confronting growing political and social pressure.

With mounting concerns over job losses, AI‑runaway risks and the high electricity consumption of data centers, construction projects are meeting increasing opposition and some Blackstone projects are being stalled.

Capital‑market worries focus on whether AI spending can be sustained. As Blackstone, Apollo Global Management, Brookfield Asset Management and KKR and other large asset managers keep ramping up AI exposure, investors may repeatedly assume the same AI risk across equities, credit and infrastructure assets.

If the AI investment cycle reverses, the shock could transmit to multiple markets simultaneously. In other words, spreading across many industry segments does not necessarily mean true risk diversification.
Schwarzman: Major technological shifts take decades to deliver value

Addressing concerns that AI investment may be overheating, Schwarzman said that major technological innovations often need several decades to fully realize economic value, and early‑stage spending does not always translate quickly into profit.

He cited electricity infrastructure as an example, noting that Thomas Edison invented the light bulb in 1882, but it took about 40 years to build the power grid needed for the bulb to become truly useful.
Schwarzman added, “Back then no one understood broadcasting, no one understood television. When the grid was being built, no one could foresee those applications.”

The grid was initially built for lighting and similar uses, but later became the foundation for emerging industries such as broadcasting and television. Schwarzman believes AI is similarly in an early stage, and its future applications and commercial value could continue to expand.
He said, “We are still in the early phase of this process.”

That is the core logic behind Blackstone’s long‑term investment in AI infrastructure: even if some projects deliver limited short‑term returns, the underlying facilities may generate broader value as the technology matures. However, long‑term prospects do not guarantee profit on every investment; balancing capital outlays, energy costs and actual demand remains a test for investors.
Discussing U.S. political polarization, Schwarzman calls for a return to the middle ground

In the interview, Schwarzman also spoke about the growing political divide in the United States. As a long‑time Republican supporter, he said the distance between political camps is widening and cross‑camp communication is becoming increasingly difficult.
He noted, “I think it’s hard for anyone in any party these days. In the past, the middle of society was quite broad, and I was part of that.”

He continued, “Now we have reached a point where people no longer want to listen to each other. I find that very regrettable and it poses a challenge for the whole country. We need to get back to a more balanced middle ground.”

From a single chance meeting with Jack Ma to an investment portfolio that spans data centers, cloud computing, chip financing and energy infrastructure, Blackstone’s AI strategy now goes far beyond merely buying tech stocks.

Schwarzman is betting on AI’s long‑term potential, but as data‑center construction faces more resistance, capital spending keeps climbing, and concerns over concentrated investment risk rise, Blackstone still has to prove that its comprehensive AI‑value‑chain approach can translate into sustained and reasonable investment returns.

items.title: 法國驚險躲過穆迪降評！10年期公債殖利率創24年高點 赤字與政治僵局成隱憂
items.title_en: France Narrowly Avoids Moody's Downgrade! 10-Year Bond Yield Hits 24-Year High, Deficit and Political Stalemate Pose Hidden Risks
paras: 法國近來深陷社會動盪，政治風險升高、公債殖利率也大幅攀升，但仍順利躲過信評機構穆迪(Moody’s Ratings)降評，暫時獲得喘息空間。
穆迪周五(23日)宣布維持這個歐元區第二大經濟體的Aa3評級，仍比垃圾級高出7個等級，與英國相同，但維持負向展望。

去年秋季陷預算爭議 標普與惠譽已先行降評

穆迪此次決定暫時維持法國評級，意味著法國的評級仍比標普全球評級(S&P Global Ratings)與惠譽評級(Fitch Ratings)高一個等級。這兩家評級機構都在2025年秋季法國預算爭議期間，調降法國的信評。
標普預定於11月27日公布最新評估。法國上個月在信評檢視中表現不佳，Scope Ratings已降評，晨星DBRS則將評級展望降至負面。
法國財政部長勒斯屈爾(Roland Lescure)周五在聲明中表示：「這項決定肯定了我國經濟的穩健性，以及政府提出的預算案具有可信度。」
針對信評展望，穆迪在報告中說：「負面展望反映出法國政治版圖日益分裂的風險升高，這種分裂可能持續妨礙該國立法機構的運作。」
穆迪表示，如果法國的政治制度能夠協助縮小財政赤字，該機構可能將法國的評級展望調整為穩定。

政治僵局加劇財政壓力 法國借貸成本攀升

法國正抗議活動而陷入動盪，上周末有超過50萬人走上街頭，表達對公共服務品質下滑及生活成本高漲的不滿。巴黎當局正努力避免大規模暴動再度發生，以免重演先前多座城市遭受嚴重破壞的情況。
穆迪周五在報告中表示：「政治不穩定也反映在當前的社會緊張局勢中，這可能妨礙法國政府處理重要政策挑戰的能力，包括偏高的財政赤字、日益沉重的債務負擔，以及借貸成本持續上升等問題，進而使該國主權信用的關鍵指標，比我們目前預期更快惡化。」
法國10年期公債殖利率本周突破5%，是2002年以來首見，法國與德國公債殖利率的利差，也升至15年來最高水準。
目前法國的財政赤字占國內生產毛額(GDP)比率約為5.5%，遠高於歐盟成員國3%的上限，而且接下來到2030年，還有逾1兆美元債務將到期，需要設法償還或再融資。
法國財政部一個月前曾警告，債務占GDP比率預料將在2027年升至121.7%。
paras_en: France has recently been mired in social unrest, with rising political risk and sharply higher sovereign bond yields, yet it has managed to dodge a downgrade from Moody's Ratings, buying itself a temporary breather.

Moody's announced on Friday the 23rd that it is maintaining the Eurozone's second‑largest economy at an Aa3 rating, still seven notches above junk status and on par with the United Kingdom, but it kept a negative outlook.

Moody's decision to keep France's rating unchanged means France's rating remains one notch higher than that of S&P Global Ratings and Fitch Ratings, both of which cut France's credit rating during the budget dispute in the autumn of 2025.

S&P is scheduled to release its latest assessment on November 27. France performed poorly in last month’s rating review, with Scope Ratings downgrading it and Morningstar DBRS shifting its outlook to negative.
French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said in a statement on Friday, "This decision confirms the soundness of our economy and the credibility of the government's budget proposal."

Regarding the rating outlook, Moody's said in its report, "The negative outlook reflects the heightened risk of an increasingly fragmented political landscape in France, a fragmentation that could continue to impede the functioning of the legislature."
Moody's added that if France's political system helps narrow the fiscal deficit, the agency could move the rating outlook to stable.
Political deadlock is intensifying fiscal pressure as France's borrowing costs climb.

Moody's noted in its Friday report, "Political instability also shows up in the current social tension, which may hinder the French government's ability to tackle key policy challenges, including an elevated fiscal deficit, a growing debt burden and rising borrowing costs, causing the sovereign credit's key indicators to deteriorate faster than we currently expect."
France's 10‑year sovereign bond yield broke the 5% mark this week, the first time since 2002, while the spread between French and German yields rose to its highest level in 15 years.
France's fiscal deficit currently stands at about 5.5% of GDP, well above the EU member‑state ceiling of 3%, and more than $1 trillion of debt will mature by 2030, requiring repayment or refinancing.
The French Treasury warned a month ago that the debt‑to‑GDP ratio is projected to rise to 121.7% by 2027.

items.title: 散戶抄底愈抄愈低！半導體槓桿ETF單周吸金61億美元 10月已暴跌逾40%
items.title_en: Retail Investors' Bottom‑Fishing Gets Deeper: Semiconductor Leveraged ETF Pulls in $6.1 B in One Week, Down Over 40% in October
paras: 人工智慧(AI)交易近期再度受挫，投資人上周試圖趁股價下跌進場，把資金投入一檔高風險槓桿型指數股票型基金(ETF)，以放大半導體股的每日報酬，但在晶片股賣壓依然沉重的情況下，試圖逢低買進的投資人也面臨虧損。
根據FactSet數據，追蹤熱門半導體指數每日漲跌幅三倍的「Direxion每日三倍做多半導體ETF」(Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF)(SOXL-US)，上周吸引創紀錄的61億美元資金流入。
然而，半導體股本周持續下跌，FactSet數據顯示，這檔槓桿ETF本周再跌10.8%，連續第三周下跌，10月迄今跌幅可能已超過43%。
換句話說，投資人原本想逢低買進，沒想到股價卻持續探底。

槓桿ETF單日重挫逾2成 AI投資回報疑慮升高

FactSet數據顯示，這檔槓桿ETF本周到周四持續有資金流入，然而周四當天半導體股遭到猛烈拋售，ETF股價也大幅下挫。
AI交易這個月每天都劇烈波動，足以左右標普500指數單日表現，令投資人感到不安。
財富管理公司Glenmede投資策略副總裁Mike Reynolds周五(23日)說：「半導體股對AI基建設置的變化極為敏感。市場目前已開始對AI交易抱持懷疑。」
投資人高度關注AI發展需要的大量晶片，使半導體公司今年來股價大幅上漲。強勁的AI晶片需求推動相關企業獲利成長，但投資人也密切關注企業的AI支出，擔心如此積極的投資步調可能難以持續。
半導體股大幅波動，也帶動投資人對槓桿ETF的熱情。這類基金利用衍生性金融商品放大股市每日報酬，但若投資人將其當作押注股價上漲的交易工具，一旦市場反向下跌，可能蒙受沉重損失。
根據FactSet數據，Direxion每日三倍做多半導體ETF周四當天重挫20.5%，創6月23日以來最差單日表現。相較之下，iShares半導體ETF(iShares Semiconductor ETF)(SOXX-US)當日下跌6.8%，跌幅較小。
FactSet數據顯示，Direxion每日三倍做多半導體ETF本月周線表現持續疲弱，截至周五已連續第三周下跌。

半導體股今年仍大漲 投資人重新評估估值

在半導體股2026年大幅上漲後，投資人正重新評估相關股票的估值。iShares半導體ETF今年以來仍大漲近59%，儘管近期半導體股再度承受賣壓。
Reynolds說：「在目前這樣的估值水準，以及經歷如此猛烈的漲勢後，投資人冷靜重新評估這項AI主題可能帶來的投資回報，是件好事。」
他也表示，投資人在市場真正陷入狂熱、股價與基本面完全脫節之前，就開始即時質疑這波行情，是有益的。
FactSet數據顯示，美股周五收低，標普500資訊科技類股連續第三周下跌，創3月以來最長連續周線跌勢。iShares半導體ETF也連續第三周下跌，10月跌幅可能達15.9%。
paras_en: AI‑driven trading has hit another snag recently. Last week investors tried to capitalize on falling prices by pouring money into a high‑risk leveraged semiconductor index fund to amplify daily returns, but with chip stocks still under heavy selling pressure, those buying the dip are also facing losses.

According to FactSet data, the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL‑US), which tracks a popular semiconductor index with three‑times daily price movements, attracted a record $6.1 billion of inflows last week.

However, semiconductor stocks kept sliding this week. FactSet shows the leveraged ETF fell another 10.8% this week, marking a third consecutive week of decline, and its October loss may already exceed 43%.
In other words, investors who hoped to buy the dip found the price continuing to plunge.

The leveraged ETF saw a single‑day plunge of over 20%, raising doubts about AI‑driven returns. FactSet data indicate that while inflows continued through Thursday, semiconductor stocks were hammered that day, dragging the ETF’s price sharply lower.
AI‑related trading has been wildly volatile all month, enough to sway the S&P 500’s daily performance and leave investors uneasy.

Mike Reynolds, vice‑president of investment strategy at wealth‑management firm Glenmede, said on Friday the 23rd that semiconductor stocks are extremely sensitive to changes in AI infrastructure spending, and the market is now growing skeptical of AI‑driven trading.

Investors have been closely watching the massive chip demand required for AI development, which has driven semiconductor shares sharply higher this year. Strong AI chip demand has boosted earnings for related firms, but investors are also watching corporate AI spending, fearing such aggressive investment may be hard to sustain.

The wild swings in semiconductor stocks have also fueled enthusiasm for leveraged ETFs. These funds use derivatives to magnify daily market returns, but if investors treat them as bets on price rises, a market reversal can inflict heavy losses.

FactSet data show the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF plunged 20.5% on Thursday, its worst single‑day performance since June 23. By contrast, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX‑US) fell 6.8% that day, a much smaller drop.
FactSet indicates the leveraged ETF’s weekly performance has remained weak this month, and by Friday it had logged a third consecutive week of decline.

Semiconductor stocks have surged dramatically this year, prompting investors to reassess valuations. The iShares Semiconductor ETF is up nearly 59% year‑to‑date, even as recent selling pressure returns to chip stocks.
Reynolds said that given current valuation levels and the recent fierce rally, it is healthy for investors to calmly re‑evaluate the potential returns of the AI theme.
He added that it is beneficial for investors to question the rally in real time before the market becomes overly frothy and prices diverge completely from fundamentals.
